description_full: United Therapeutics Corporation engages in the development and commercialization of products to address the unmet medical needs of patients with chronic and life-threatening diseases in the United States and internationally. It offers Tyvaso DPI, an inhaled dry powder via pre-filled and single-use cartridges; Nebulized Tyvaso, an inhaled solution via ultrasonic nebulizer; Remodulin (treprostinil) injection to treat patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension to diminish symptoms associated with exercise; Orenitram, a tablet dosage form of treprostinil, to delay disease progression and improve exercise capacity in PAH patients; and Adcirca, an oral PDE-5 inhibitor to enhance the exercise ability in PAH patients. It also markets and sells Unituxin (dinutuximab) injection, a monoclonal antibody for high-risk neuroblastoma; and Remunity Pump, which contains a pump and separate controller for Remodulin. In addition, it is involved in developing RemunityPRO Pump and Ralinepag for the treatment of PAH;and Nebulized Tyvaso, for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, as well as xenografts, which are development-stage organ products. Further, it provides preclinical products, including EVLP/CLES, for lung transplant; UKidney, UHeart, UThymoKidney, a development-stage gene-edited porcine kidneys and hearts for xenotransplantation; ULobe, for allogeneic regenerative medicine; ULung, for autologous regenerative medicine; IVIVA Kidney, for autologous regenerative medicine; miroliver, for allogeneic regenerative medicine; and mirokidney, for allogeneic regenerative medicine. It has licensing and collaboration agreements with DEKA Research & Development Corp. to develop a semi-disposable system for the subcutaneous delivery of treprostinil; MannKind Corporation to develop and license treprostinil inhalation powder and the Dreamboat device; and Arena Pharmaceuticals, Inc. to develop Ralinepag. The company was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Silver Spring, Maryland.

financial_summary: United Therapeutics Corporation is a large-cap healthcare business with a $23.6B market cap on $3.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +18% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 35% against a 9% cost of capital — a 26-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 89% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.0B in free cash flow — roughly 33 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.17× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 77× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.1% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 5.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 47% operating margin runs 47pp above the Healthcare median (0%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 5.33x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+11.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 465 companies in the universe; the top four hold 35% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 17% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 10% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 35% and a beta of 0.69, it is more defensive than the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $291.8M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 31% in the 2020 crash, 22% in the 2022 bear market and 58% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 15% below its DCF fair value of $656, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 8%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $511 to $870 (P10-P90).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 46% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 14 covering analysts target $687 on average, 24% above the price.
The price implies 5.1% annual cash-flow growth, 3pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 35% clears the cost of capital of 8.5% by 26pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.57).
It runs a 89% gross margin and converts 33% of revenue into free cash flow, or 28% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.17x.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.1x equity multiplier).
It spends 17.3% of revenue on R&D and 4.6% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.9B (12% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 21.1, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 207 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 18.0% over 3 years, 16.5% over 5 years and 8.1% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 38% of profits supports about 13.2% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 8.4% a year over five years.
Capex runs 6.1x depreciation (16.4% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.1%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (186 sales, net $59.5M sold).
It returns 4.2% a year to shareholders (4.2% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 1,400 employees, each generates about $2.3M of revenue, 6.0x the Healthcare median, and revenue has grown 11.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $743K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $5.8M (3x revenue per employee).
